title: Life Expectancy and Inequality — TikTok
notes: Story follows the article's arc: the 20-year gap → Oglala Lakota → money decides → the map → Summit vs Oglala → Chetty's tax records → falling life expectancy in Kentucky → healthcare costs → born in the wrong county.
All figures are from the article (Feb 2, 2021) and the sources it cites (GHDx, Chetty et al., World Bank).

post.headline: Where you're born can cost you 20 years of life
post.caption: People in America's richest counties now outlive the poorest by up to 20 years. In Oglala Lakota County, South Dakota, life expectancy is 66.8. In Colorado's Summit County it's 86.9. The richest 1% of men outlive the poorest 1% by 14.6 years.
post.cta: Full story and interactive maps at the link in bio.

headline.text: The richest counties outlive the poorest by {20 years.}

say: Rich counties outlive the poorest by up to 20 years.

overlays.label: years, life expectancy in Oglala Lakota County

say: In Oglala Lakota County, South Dakota, life expectancy is just 66.8 years, the lowest in America.
Money has become an increasingly strong determinant of who will live longer.

scenes.source: Global Health Data Exchange · American Inequality
say: America now has its greatest gap in life expectancy across regions in 40 years.

scenes.title: Life expectancy
say: In Colorado's Summit County, people live to 86.9, and median income is more than 2.5 times higher than in Oglala Lakota.

scenes.title: Years the richest 1% outlive the poorest 1%
scenes.source: Chetty et al., 1.4 billion tax records (1999–2014)
say: Across 1.4 billion tax records, the richest 1% of men outlive the poorest 1% by 14.6 years, and for women it's 10.1.

scenes.title: Years of life gained by men, 2001–2014
say: From 2001 to 2014, the richest men gained 2.3 years of life while the poorest gained just a third of a year.
Since 1980, 13 counties have seen life expectancy fall, and 8 of them are in Kentucky.

scenes.title: Healthcare spending per person
say: Healthcare in America costs $10,624 per person, more than double the UK, Japan, and Canada.
If Americans cannot afford the cost of healthcare, they will die earlier without that care.

scenes.text: Where you're born shouldn't {cost you 20 years.}
say: We cannot allow some people to lose 20 years of their life just because they were born in one county and not another.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
